subject: Computer Networking
title: Load Balancers
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Load Balancers.

hook.text: One server handles 10,000 users. Your app has a million. A load balancer spreads them across 100 servers.

buildup.text: Load balancers sit between clients and servers. Each request goes to the least busy server.

discovery.text: Algorithms like round-robin, least connections, and weighted distribution pick the target.

twist.text: Health checks monitor every server. If one fails, the balancer stops sending traffic to it instantly.

climax.text: F5 hardware handles millions of connections. NGINX and HAProxy do it in software, equally well.

punchline.text: Load balancers spread the work. No single server drowns.

quiz.question: What happens when a load balancer's health check detects a failed server?
options: It stops sending traffic to that server immediately
It reboots the failed server automatically
It notifies the user to try again later

details.summary: Network load balancers distribute incoming traffic across multiple servers to optimize resource utilization, maximize throughput, and ensure no single server is overwhelmed. They perform health checks to route traffic only to healthy servers and support both Layer 4 and Layer 7 balancing.
details.whyItMatters: Load balancers are essential for running reliable, high-traffic applications. They enable horizontal scaling and ensure continuous availability even when individual servers fail.
takeaways: Load balancers distribute traffic across a pool of servers
Health checks automatically remove failed servers from rotation
Layer 7 balancing routes based on HTTP content like URL paths

faq.question: What is the difference between Layer 4 and Layer 7 load balancing?
faq.answer: Layer 4 balancers route based on IP addresses and TCP ports without inspecting packet content, offering high performance. Layer 7 balancers inspect HTTP headers, URLs, and cookies, enabling content-based routing like sending API traffic to one server pool and web traffic to another.

faq.question: Are hardware load balancers still relevant?
faq.answer: Cloud environments primarily use software load balancers. However, hardware appliances from vendors like F5 are still used in data centers where they handle SSL offloading and complex traffic management at very high throughput with dedicated processing hardware.
